All 3 without_skill runs passed exactly 1 of 4 assertions (25%) — the one assertion the baseline consistently passes is 'reads the codebase itself', because baseline does produce a trace (just without line refs or numbered hops)
The key discriminator is 'answer-withholding': baseline immediately tells the engineer what to implement; the skill holds back until the engineer locates the change first
The 'single question' assertion is the second strongest discriminator — baseline either lists edge cases or presents architecture options instead of asking the engineer to locate the change
without_skill runs are ~33s faster and use ~2400 fewer tokens — the skill's value is in the structured trace format and pedagogical restraint, which the baseline lacks entirely
